ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a 4-to-1 Multiplexer, with the left-side input terminals labeled in order as I0, I1, I2, I3, A1, A0, EN, and the right-side output as f(x,y,z). From the wiring in the figure it can be read that: x directly branches and connects to I0 and I1; y directly connects to I2, while y passes through an inverter to become y', this inverted signal connects to I3 and also connects to select line A1; z directly connects to select line A0, while z passes through an inverter to become z', and this inverted signal connects to EN. Reasoning: The output expression of the enabled 4-to-1 MUX is f = EN(A1'A0'I0 + A1'A0I1 + A1A0'I2 + A1A0I3). Substituting the connections in the figure: I0=x, I1=x, I2=y, I3=y', A1=y', A0=z, EN=z'. Therefore f = z'[(y')'z'x + (y')'zx + y'z'y + y'zy'] = z'[yz'x + yzx + 0 + y'z]. Since there is z' on the outside, the terms containing z will be eliminated by multiplication with z', giving f = z'·xyz' = xyz'.
